audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet Jehoram, Moab revolt, Elisha oracle, and Mesha child-sacrifice narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Jehoram's reign, Mesha's tribute and rebellion, Israel-Judah-Edom coalition, wilderness water crisis, Elisha's musician-assisted oracle, Moabite misreading of water, city destruction, and king of Moab's sacrifice of his son.

verses.restored: Jehoram son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned twelve years.
He did evil in eyes of YHWH, though not like his father and mother; he removed pillar of Baal his father had made.
Yet he clung to sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin; he did not turn from them.
Mesha king of Moab was a sheep breeder, and he returned to king of Israel one hundred thousand lambs and wool of one hundred thousand rams.
When Ahab died, king of Moab rebelled against king of Israel.
King Jehoram went out from Samaria at that time and mustered all Israel.

He sent to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, saying, King of Moab has rebelled against me; will you go with me to Moab for war? He said, I will go; I am as you, my people as your people, my horses as your horses.
He said, Which way shall we go up? He answered, Way of wilderness of Edom.
King of Israel, king of Judah, and king of Edom went; after seven days circling, there was no water for army or animals at their feet.
King of Israel said, Alas, YHWH has called these three kings to give them into hand of Moab.
Jehoshaphat said, Is there no prophet of YHWH here, that we may inquire of YHWH by him? One servant answered, Elisha son of Shaphat is here, who poured water on hands of Elijah.
Jehoshaphat said, Word of YHWH is with him. So king of Israel, Jehoshaphat, and king of Edom went down to him.
Elisha said to king of Israel, What is there between me and you? Go to prophets of your father and mother. King of Israel said, No, for YHWH called these three kings to give them into hand of Moab.
Elisha said, As YHWH of hosts lives, before whom I stand, if I did not lift face of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not look toward you or see you.
Now bring me a musician. When musician played, hand of YHWH came upon him.
He said, Thus says YHWH: Make this wadi pits, pits.
For thus says YHWH: You shall not see wind and shall not see rain, yet that wadi shall be filled with water, and you shall drink, you, your livestock, and your animals.
This is light in eyes of YHWH; he will also give Moab into your hand.
You shall strike every fortified city and every choice city; every good tree you shall fell, all springs of water stop up, and every good field ruin with stones.
In morning, at time of offering, look, water came from way of Edom, and land was filled with water.
All Moab heard kings had come to fight them; all able to gird armor and upward were called and stood at border.
They rose early, and sun shone upon water; Moab saw water opposite them red as blood.
They said, This is blood; the kings have surely fought each other. Now to spoil, Moab!
They came to camp of Israel, and Israel rose and struck Moab; they fled before them, and Israel entered, striking Moab.

They destroyed cities, and each man threw stone on every good field until it was covered; they stopped every spring and felled every good tree, until only Kir-hareseth stones remained. Slingers surrounded and struck it.
King of Moab saw battle was too strong for him; he took with him seven hundred men drawing sword to break through to king of Edom, but they could not.
He took his firstborn son who would reign after him and brought him up as an ascending offering on the wall. Great wrath came upon Israel, and they withdrew from him and returned to land.

translation_notes: Mesha's tribute and rebellion should be compared with the Mesha Stele; the biblical account is a Judah/Israel-facing war memory, not the only witness.
The coalition's lack of water includes animals; war logistics place human and nonhuman bodies at risk.
Elisha's use of a musician before prophecy preserves a connection between sound and inspired speech without creating a formula for forced prophecy.
Verse 19 commands ecological warfare: felling trees, stopping springs, and ruining fields. This must be rejected as a modern environmental or military model.
The red-water misunderstanding drives Moab into disaster; perception under war conditions can be lethal.
Verse 27 reports the king of Moab sacrificing his heir on the wall. This is child sacrifice under siege desperation and royal violence, not devotion to be imitated.
The great wrath that follows is ambiguous; do not use it to validate child sacrifice or claim human sacrifice has spiritual power.
safety_note: Do not use 2 Kings 3 to justify ecological warfare, child sacrifice, siege tactics, anti-Moabite hatred, animal neglect, or claims that desperate ritual violence works. Keep the son on the wall visible as a child and heir destroyed by royal war.
